_about:
Event write-ups written for GeoHistory (AI-written from the sources listed with each entry; shown in the
app with that label). One JSON file per batch in t1/. Each entry, keyed by the event id of data/events:

  "title", "y" (must equal the event's year), "place" (as in the event record),
  "paras": 2-5 short paragraphs (who and on which side; what happened, step by step; why; what it led to),
  "sources": [{"url", "title", "publisher", "accessed", "supports": [claim numbers]}]  every URL was fetched,
  "claims": ["claim 1", ...]  the factual claims in the text, numbered from 1, each supported by a source,
  "disagree": where sources differ (also said in the text), or null,
  "checked": null, or {"by": source url not used for writing, "result": "...", "errors": n} after the
             random re-check.

Britannica (403), the Oxford DNB (403), the Imperial War Museums (403), the British Museum (403) and
Smithsonian Magazine (403) refuse automated fetches from this build's network, so they are not cited.
Text is never copied from copyrighted pages; Wikipedia text is summarised with attribution.
_process: Checks before an entry is added: (1) every claim is matched to a source that was fetched (tools/context/writeup_add.py checks the numbering); (2) every claim backed by one source only is searched for in the other source's text, and every date or number found in only one source must be confirmed in Wikipedia or a third fetched source, or stated as that source's figure, or removed; a flagged date is never kept on memory alone (rule added after two errors in re-checks, both single-source HISTORY.com dates); (3) a re-check of at least 2% of each batch's claims against a source not used for writing, recorded in 'checked'; if a batch's re-check error rate is above 2%, writing stops until the process is fixed. (4) Figures that differ between sources are never merged into an unattributed range or round number; each is given with its source (rule added after the fifth batch of 2026-11-28, whose re-check found an unattributed army-size range at Solferino contradicted by a third source: 1 error in 25 claims). (5) What a vow, decree, treaty or document contained (its terms, its list of points, who swore to what) is confirmed in a second fetched source or attributed to its one source, and when a cited second source covers the same point it is compared, not only searched for numbers (rule added after the fourteenth batch of 2026-11-28, whose re-check found the Montmartre vows of 1534 given from Wikipedia as poverty, chastity and obedience, where the Catholic Encyclopedia names poverty and chastity and the 1911 Britannica dates the vow of obedience to 1539: 1 error in 23 claims; the batch's other such claims were then attributed). (6) Anecdotes, famous sayings and vows (who said or swore what), and any episode that a fetched source itself calls disputed, are attributed to their source in the text unless two independent fetched sources agree and no fetched source disputes them (rule added after the sixteenth batch of 2026-11-28, whose re-check found the 'win or die' vow at the Monte Negino redoubt given as Rampon's, following Wikipedia and the 1911 Britannica, while Rose's Life of Napoleon I, citing the documents, gives the words to Colonel Fornesy: 1 error in 24 claims; the batch's other such passages were then attributed).
